task.description:
Write test/specs/REQ-025.md and test/letflow/event_store_test.exs for Letflow.EventStore.append/2, which just passed SECURITY-REVIEWER and REVIEWER (both re-validated after a rework: 2 SECURITY-REVIEWER INV-8 iterations on struct-shaped metadata crashing validate_metadata/1, then a REVIEWER FAIL on OQ-5 requiring a design change to M1/M6's instance_projections contract). Read lib/letflow/design/req025-event-append.md in full before writing anything -- it is now update-only for instance_projections, not the create-if-absent design REQ-025's own requirement text vaguely implies.

CRITICAL, read this before writing any fixture: per the design's now-RESOLVED §9 OQ-5 and REVIEWER's Step 2d ruling, append/2 NEVER creates an instance_projections row -- it only updates one that already exists. M1 (active_instance_guard/3) fails the whole call with {:error, :instance_not_started} if no row exists for the target instance_id. This means EVERY test exercising append/2's success path (and the terminated-instance failure path, which also needs an existing row) MUST pre-seed an instance_projections row directly via Repo.insert(%InstanceProjection{...}, prefix: schema_name) in test setup -- never via append/2 itself. Also write at least one explicit test for the NEW failure mode: calling append/2 against an instance_id with no pre-existing instance_projections row returns {:error, :instance_not_started} and writes zero rows anywhere (this is a new acceptance-criteria-adjacent behavior introduced by the OQ-5 rework, not literally named in docs/requirements.yaml's original AC list, but load-bearing -- REVIEWER will expect it covered).

Cover REQ-025's 6 acceptance criteria (docs/requirements.yaml:1094-1099), each needing a real Postgres-backed test (docker-compose Postgres already running, per this run's prior steps -- ELIXIR-DEV's own verification ran directly against it):
1. Appending to a terminated instance (status :completed or :cancelled in a pre-seeded instance_projections row) returns {:error, {:instance_terminated, status}} and writes zero rows across all five tables.
2. Two concurrent appends to the same instance_id (pre-seeded, active) never receive the same sequence_number -- use Task.async_stream or Task.await_many racing two real append/2 calls against the same instance_id.
3. Appending twice with the same idempotency_key returns is_duplicate: true on the second call and does not insert a second events row.
4. A payload that fails Registry.validate_payload/3 results in zero rows written to events, instance_sequence, or instance_projections.
5. A payload over 4096 bytes is split into events.payload's $ref pointer form plus an event_payload_store row, verified by reading both rows back.
6. Every row append/2 writes has tenant_id equal to the tenant whose schema the write targeted (derived internally) -- per the design doc's §9 OQ-1 resolution (already validator-confirmed correct), instance_sequence and event_idempotency carry NO tenant_id column at all (schema-per-tenant boundary is their isolation mechanism instead) -- adapt AC6's test for those two tables to a prefix-reachability check (row only exists/reachable under the correct tenant's schema prefix) rather than asserting a tenant_id column value that doesn't exist. For events/instance_projections (which DO have the column), assert the column value directly, and separately assert that attrs containing a caller-supplied :tenant_id key that disagrees with the target schema is rejected with {:error, :tenant_id_not_accepted} (not silently ignored, not silently honored).

Plus the :instance_not_started case described above as a 7th, load-bearing test even though it's not literally one of the 6 listed ACs.

Use per-test unique instance_id/tenant fixtures (no shared hardcoded IDs), matching this project's established property-test/fixture conventions elsewhere in test/letflow/. Every test must be self-sufficient (no dependency on execution order).
acceptance_criteria: appending to a terminated instance (status CANCELLED or COMPLETED in instance_projections) returns an error and writes zero rows across all five involved tables, demonstrated by an actual test or iex session against a real Postgres, not just described

two concurrent appends to the same instance_id never receive the same sequence_number -- demonstrated with an actual concurrent test (e.g. Task.async_stream racing two appends) or, if concurrency can't be exercised in this environment, the FOR UPDATE-equivalent locking code path is cited explicitly
appending twice with the same idempotency_key returns is_duplicate: true on the second call and does not insert a second events row, verified against the idempotency sidecar table REQ-023 defines
a payload that fails REQ-024's validate_payload/2 results in zero rows written to events, instance_sequence, or instance_projections -- no partial state
a payload over 4096 bytes is split into events.payload's $ref pointer form plus an event_payload_store row, verified by reading both rows back after append

every row append/1(2) writes (events, instance_sequence, instance_projections, the idempotency sidecar) has tenant_id equal to the tenant whose schema the write targeted, derived internally -- not equal to a caller-supplied tenant_id when the two are deliberately made to disagree in a test, which must fail loudly (not silently attribute to the wrong tenant) rather than succeed

an append against an instance_id with no pre-existing instance_projections row returns {:error, :instance_not_started} and writes zero rows -- the behavior introduced by REVIEWER's Step 2d OQ-5 ruling

result.summary:
Wrote test/specs/REQ-025.md (fixture strategy stated up front: every test that needs append/2 to reach its transactional phase pre-seeds instance_projections via a direct Repo.insert, never via append/2 -- the REVIEWER-confirmed strategy design doc §6.2.1/§9 OQ-5 name explicitly) and test/letflow/event_store_test.exs (10 tests, 8 describe blocks, one per acceptance criterion plus the 7th :instance_not_started case).

Fixture pattern: reused registry_test.exs's/tenant_provisioning_test.exs's established provisioned_tenant/1 helper verbatim in shape (real CREATE SCHEMA via TenantProvisioning.provision_tenant_schema/1, real tenant_scoped_migrations/0 replay via TenantProvisioning.replay_migrations/1 -- which now includes all six REQ-023 event-store tables plus REQ-024's event_type_registry, so one provisioned_tenant/1 call is enough), Sandbox :auto mode + manual on_exit/1 cleanup (Ecto.Migrator needs a second real connection the DataCase sandbox can't hand out), async: false for the whole module. Every instance_id/idempotency_key/event-type name is per-test unique (Ecto.UUID.generate()/System.unique_integer([:positive, :monotonic])) -- no shared hardcoded fixtures, no test-order dependency.

Coverage:
- AC1 (terminated instance): 2 tests (:completed, :cancelled). Asserts zero rows in events/instance_sequence/event_idempotency/event_payload_store AND that the pre-seeded instance_projections row is byte-identical before/after (not just 'still exists').
- AC2 (concurrency): real Task-based race against the identical pre-seeded instance_id, distinct idempotency_keys per task (so the idempotency path can't collapse the race), a barrier (send/receive :go) forcing genuine overlap, Sandbox :auto mode giving each Task its own real connection (mirrors registry_test.exs's own concurrent-race precedent). Asserts both calls succeed with distinct sequence_number and exactly 2 events rows land.
- AC3 (idempotency): same idempotency_key twice -- second call returns is_duplicate: true, same event_id/sequence_number as the first, exactly 1 events row and 1 event_idempotency row (the strictly-stronger INV-AP-6 property, not just 'no second events row').
- AC7/instance_not_started: deliberately no seed_projection!/4 call -- asserts {:error, :instance_not_started} and zero rows anywhere.
- AC4 (invalid payload): a JSON-Schema-required-field violation, deliberately without a pre-seeded instance_projections row either -- proves Registry validation (design doc §6.1 P4) runs entirely pre-transaction and is never masked by/conflated with :instance_not_started.
- AC5 (oversized payload): a >4096-byte payload; asserts events.payload == %{"$ref" => event_id} and reads the event_payload_store row back directly from Postgres (payload + byte_size), re-selecting the events row too rather than trusting the in-memory reply.
- AC6 (tenant_id), 3 sub-tests: (a) events/instance_projections tenant_id equals TenantProvisioning.tenant_id_for_schema_name/1's independently-computed result (not a tautological re-check of the fixture's own value); (b) instance_sequence/event_idempotency (which the shipped schema confirms carry no tenant_id column) checked via cross-tenant schema-prefix reachability -- a second, genuinely provisioned tenant's prefix genuinely returns nil; (c) attrs carrying a disagreeing :tenant_id key rejected with {:error, :tenant_id_not_accepted}, zero rows written.

Ran mix compile --warnings-as-errors (MIX_ENV=test, forced recompile): 'Compiling 51 files (.ex) / Generated letflow app' -- clean, zero warnings (one iteration fixed: seed_projection!/4's status argument had an unused default value since every call site passes it explicitly -- removed the default, re-verified clean). mix format --check-formatted test/letflow/event_store_test.exs: exit 0.

Ran mix test test/letflow/event_store_test.exs --seed 0 against the real docker-compose Postgres already running on this host: '10 tests, 0 failures' (confirmed twice, before and after the unused-default fix, both green).
